name: Aleniglipron
lead: Aleniglipron (development code GSBR-1290) is an investigational oral, small-molecule glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist being developed for obesity and overweight. Unlike injectable peptide GLP-1 drugs such as semaglutide, it is a non-peptide pill taken once daily. [1][2]

In the ACCESS phase 2b trial, 230 adults with obesity or overweight received aleniglipron or placebo for 36 weeks. Placebo-adjusted weight change was -8.2%, -9.8% and -11.3% at the 45, 90 and 120 mg arms respectively. Gastrointestinal events were generally mild to moderate, and treatment-related discontinuations were 10.4% across drug arms, with no drug-induced liver injury reported. [1]
The drug is not approved. Phase 3 trials (ACCOMPLISH-1 and ACCOMPLISH-2) began registering participants in 2026. [3][4]

paras: Aleniglipron activates the GLP-1 receptor, the same target as injectable agents used for weight management. Small-molecule agonists are a distinct chemical class from peptides; a structural review notes four known chemotypes of small-molecule GLP-1R agonists, which offer potential advantages in accessibility and patient convenience compared with peptide agonists. [5]

The ACCESS phase 2b trial (NCT06693843) was randomised, double-blind and placebo-controlled. Participants had a mean BMI of 39.5 and received once-daily aleniglipron, escalated every 4 weeks to 45, 90 or 120 mg. At week 36 all doses significantly outperformed placebo on the primary endpoint, with no apparent weight-loss plateau, and an interim look at the open-label extension showed continued weight loss. Vomiting rarely recurred after reintroduction following permitted dose interruptions. [1][6] A publisher correction to the paper has been issued. [7]

Additional phase 2 studies in people with type 2 diabetes, a body-composition study and a dose-range study have been registered as completed. [8][9][10] A pooled analysis of randomised trials of oral non-peptide GLP-1 agonists in people without diabetes, posted as a preprint, examines the class as a whole. [11]
Phase 3 trials are recruiting: ACCOMPLISH-1 (3,600 participants with obesity or overweight and a weight-related condition) and ACCOMPLISH-2 (1,100 participants with type 2 diabetes). [3][4]

In ACCESS the reported tolerability profile was consistent with the GLP-1 receptor agonist class: gastrointestinal events were typically mild to moderate and became less frequent over time. No drug-induced liver injury was reported. [1] A dedicated hepatic impairment pharmacokinetic study is registered. [12]

timeline.event: ACCESS results published in Nature Medicine; phase 3 ACCOMPLISH trials start. [1][3][4]

card.summary: An experimental once-daily GLP-1 pill that cut weight by about 8-11% (placebo-adjusted) over 36 weeks in phase 2b.
card.note: Investigational and not approved; phase 3 under way.

quick.overview:
Aleniglipron is an experimental oral GLP-1 agonist for obesity. It is a once-daily small-molecule pill rather than an injectable peptide.

In a 36-week phase 2b trial of 230 adults, placebo-adjusted weight loss ranged from 8.2% to 11.3% depending on dose. Phase 3 trials started in 2026.
quick.mechanism: It activates the GLP-1 receptor, the pathway used by semaglutide and similar drugs that reduces appetite and food intake. Being a non-peptide, it can be taken by mouth.
quick.risks: Gastrointestinal events were the main adverse effects and were mostly mild to moderate; 10.4% of drug-arm participants stopped treatment for treatment-related reasons, and no drug-induced liver injury was reported. It is not approved and long-term data are lacking.
